Sample Description: Welcome to the Final Fantasy Sound Sources spreadsheet! This spreadsheet aims to provide comprehensive documentation for the sources of sounds used in Final Fantasy games.

We only ask that you do not claim this information as your own. This information is freely available for anyone to share and discuss: 
For crediting, this documentation is managed by the VGM Resources community and the various communities related to it.
Some of the findings on this sheet derive from the NEWER VGM Sound Sources spreadsheet, linked on this cell.
General Spreadsheet Editor Rules
1. Only list confirmed sources.
Sample #: List all known instruments in the track. Instruments with known sound sources should be verified beyond reasonable doubt, preferably with a demo. If the source is unknown, add "UNKNOWN" under the "Source" column.

Sample Description: 2. Do not reinterpret patch names.
Sample #: Write patch/preset names exactly how they are displayed on the product or patch list in question. Do not abbreviate*, expand, reorder, or attempt to clarify the patch name in any way. Use the notes section if you must append any clarifications.

Sample Description: 3. Handle disputes correctly.
Sample #: Place a comment on the sheet if you are challenging a find (particularly those without audio demonstrations), and put important developments in the comment thread. Do not erase the entry until the dispute is resolved.

Spreadsheet Editor Rules
1. List findings in order of sample number.
Sample #: List each finding in order of which each sample comes in in the game's soundbank.

Sample Description: 2. List which articulation was sampled.
Sample #: Using brackets, list which articulation was sampled for an instrument next to its preset (ex. Trumpet [stac]).

Sample Description: 3. For drums, list which key was sampled.
Sample #: Using brackets, list which key of a drum kit was sampled next to its preset (ex. Power Set 2 [Note D#]).

Sample Description: 4. Use the C-1-G9 note range.
Sample #: Many people use FL Studio, where C0 is the bottom note. If that's the case, simply transpose each key an octave down.

SNES Era (IV-VI, Mystic Quest) editor guidlines
1. Provide a description of the sample
2. List by Sample ID
Sample #: Try to list files in order of their in-game index.

Sample Description: 3. Use official English translations
Sample #: Square Enix has released the OSTs to all their mainline Final Fantasy games. For FFV (which never saw it or its OST get an official release outside Japan), use their literal translations, as that is what has remained consistent in suplementary material.

Sample Description: Final Fantasy X, X-2, XI editor guidlines
1. List by OST placement, then list sample by Sample #
2. Provide a description of the sample
Sample #: This is so that keeping track of what needs to be found easier. The best way to get a description of a sound is via the soundfont rips by Exabyte U, albeit its not perfect sometimes.

Sample Description: Final Fantasy Tactics Advance, Finest Fantasy
1. There are two sections
Sample #: The OST splits it in two discs: Disc 1 is the sequenced music. Disc 2 is the streamed music. The tracks on Disc 2 should be formatted like XII+

Sample Description: DS Games editor guidelines
1. List sections by .SWAR name.
Sample #: List sections by .SWAR (wave archive) name, and include any tracks that use them in parentheses (try to use the OST track names, with some exceptions). List entries by .SWAV number.

Sample Description: 2. List sections in order of their internal ID.
Sample #: Each .SWAR has an internal ID. You can check these by opening a game's .SDAT file with software like NitroStudio.

Sample Description: Streamed music (FFXII+, most spin-offs) editor guidelines
1. Use official English translations
Sample #: Some OSTs streaming releases (such as XIII) use Japanese instead of the English title. For games without an official OST release (or an incomplete OST release), use literal Japanese translations until an official release.

Sample Description: 2. List ALL instruments heard in the track.
Sample #: List all sounds in a track, even if the source is unknown. That way, it makes finding these samples easier.

Sample Description: 3. Seperate sequels from the main game
Sample #: For games with direct sequels, those sequels should be listed separately in their own section. Exceptions are made with DLC/Expansions (XIV, XV, etc.). Spin-off series (like Crystal Chronicles, Chocobo, Dissidia, etc.) should be listed after the most recent mainline entry, to which they are then ordered chronologically
